IndusTech Corporation - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the IndusTech Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to request through the phone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss IndusTech Corporation's results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; David Hargrove, Chief Financial Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena.

Elena Vasquez (CEO):
Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on IndusTech Corporation's performance for the third quarter. We've made significant progress on several fronts, positioning us strongly in the industrial equipment landscape. First, our automation and digital offerings have been a standout growth engine, delivering substantial revenue increases and efficiency gains for both our customers and operations. Second, demand trends across our key end markets—construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing—remain robust overall, supported by infrastructure tailwinds and reshoring. Third, our total order intake hit impressive levels with solid year-over-year growth, bolstering our backlog. Fourth, we've seen continued positive trends in gross and operating margins through mix shifts and cost discipline. And fifth, we're guiding for operating margin expansion in the coming quarter and full year, reflecting our strategic execution.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David to provide more detail on our financial results.

David Hargrove (CFO):
Thank you, Elena. Turning to our financial performance, IndusTech Corporation reported $1.3 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 32.8%, driven by favorable product mix, pricing discipline, and moderating raw material costs. Operating expenses were $254 million, resulting in an operating income of $172 million. Our net income for the quarter was $130 million, or $1.85 per diluted share.

We are reaffirming our guidance for the full year, with expected revenue growth of 7% to 9% and EPS of $4.85 to $5.15. We are committed to returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Before handing over to Raj for an operational update, let me expand on some of these key drivers that Elena highlighted, as they underscore our momentum.

Starting with our automation and digital offerings, this segment is transforming our business model toward higher-margin, recurring revenue while delivering real efficiency gains in the manufacturing and industrial equipment space. In Q3, it generated $285 million in revenue, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, outpacing our overall company growth and now comprising 22% of total revenue, up from 17% last year. Hardware automation, including collaborative robots or cobots and advanced PLCs, grew 18% to $140 million. But digital offerings—software, SaaS subscriptions, and analytics—surged 42% to $145 million, with annual recurring revenue reaching $520 million, a 35% jump, and a net retention rate of 118%, showing customers expanding spend by nearly 20% annually.

This rides strong industry tailwinds, with the global industrial automation market headed toward $320 billion by 2027, accelerated by digital twins and AI/ML adoption. Customers are embracing Industry 4.0 to tackle labor shortages—a projected 2.1 million worker gap in U.S. manufacturing by 2030—and supply chain issues. Our predictive maintenance via IoT edge computing cuts unplanned downtime by up to 40%, and AI-optimized scheduling boosts throughput by 25%.

At the heart is our IndusEdge Platform, our IIoT ecosystem integrating with legacy systems like Rockwell's FactoryTalk or Siemens' MindSphere. It now connects over 15,000 assets at 2,500 sites, featuring real-time digital twins with NVIDIA Omniverse tech that reduces prototyping CAPEX by 30%, and our GenAI copilot, IndusAI Assist, which analyzes SCADA data for process tweaks, trimming energy use by 15-20% in high-volume lines.

Take our FlexLine Cobot Series, integrating ROS2 for easy deployment—we shipped 1,200 units in Q3, up 50%, with ASPs steady at $85,000 via bundled services. A Midwest Tier-1 automotive supplier retrofitted stamping lines, lifting OEE from 78% to 92%, saving $4.2 million annually per plant.

Regionally, North America took 45% of sales at $128 million, up 32%, leveraging reshoring in EV batteries and semiconductor fabs, with EBITDA margins up 450 bps to 38% on 65% service attach rates. Europe, 30% at $85 million up 25%, aligns with ESG via solutions like EcoForge Optimizer, helping a German steel producer cut CO2 by 18% and boost yields 12%; digital ARR grew 48%. Asia-Pacific, 25% at $72 million up 27%, taps China's semi boom and India's PLI, with vision-guided robots hitting 99.8% defect detection; Singapore production keeps lead times under 8 weeks.

For customers, we've delivered $1.2 billion in aggregate savings since 2021, doubling MTBF to 18 months and dropping repair times 35% with AR diagnostics, per ARC Advisory audits. Internally, segment gross margins hit 52% versus company 38%, OPEX fell 300 bps to 22% with scalable cloud on AWS Outposts under 50ms latency, and FCF was $95 million, funding 15% of our 8.5% R&D on quantum-safe OT cyber and 5G wireless. We're investing $450 million from cash flow into a $2.1 billion backlog up 40%, including a $180 million Danish digital twin acquisition and ABB co-development for oil & gas skids. We expect 25-30% segment growth in FY24, digital to 50% mix by 2026, gaining on Fanuc and Yaskawa as capex rebounds.

Next, on demand trends in our key end markets—construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing—overall demand is healthy, driven by infrastructure, commodities, and reshoring, though tempered by rates and China softness. Our backlog is $4.2 billion, up 18%, with 1.25x book-to-bill.

Construction, 42% of revenues, eyes mid-teens FY24 growth. North America shines with IIJA projects boosting excavator and wheel loader orders 22%, utilization at 85% via telematics on 50,000 machines; non-residential spend up 12% on data centers. EMEA mixed—UK/Middle East megaprojects up 15%, Germany PMI at 42; APAC dipped 5% on China property but offset by SE Asia rail. Our NextGen hybrids cut fuel 25%, emissions 40%.

Mining, 28%, grew 20% on copper over $4.50/lb, gold $2,000/oz; autonomous haul trucks backlog up 30%, utilization 92%. Wins like $250M Peruvian battery-electric trucks; Australia/LatAm strong, IntelliMine AI cuts cycles 15%, OPEX 12%. Targeting 25% battery-electric share by 2026.

Agriculture, 18%, flat on droughts but precision ag up 14%; NA +7% on acres, Brazil +12%. FarmOS platform boosts yields 10-15%, 20% input savings.

Manufacturing, 12%, +16% on reshoring; U.S. CHIPS orders +25%, SmartFactory cobots 99.9% uptime, down 30%. NA/LatAm +20%, EMEA +8%, APAC +3%; 40% orders low-carbon, M&A for digital to 25% EBITDA by 2025.

Turning to total order intake, it reached $1.28 billion in Q3, up 18% from $1.085 billion last year, beating our 12-15% guide and strongest since Q4 2021. Book-to-bill 1.25x. Aftermarket parts up 22% to $285M.

Automation & Robotics: $685M, +25%, $120M Magna-like cobot order, AI vision 30% faster cycles. Heavy Equipment: $425M, +14%, $75M e-comm electric forklifts, 20% lower TCO. Energy & Infra: $170M, +8%, $45M wind tooling.

Regions: NA 42% $538M +28% on CHIPS; APAC 32% $410M +15% India infra; EMEA 18% $230M flat; RoW 8% $102M LatAm mining. Backlog $4.2B +22%, 9 months visibility. TitanEdge in 65% orders cuts downtime 25%; U.S. castings 40%. Mid-teens FY25 growth.

On gross and operating margin trends, gross hit 32.8% Q3, +210 bps YoY/+40 bps seq., TTM 32.1%, six quarters expanding. Mix/pricing: aftermarket 28% rev +18%, 4-6% hikes, 95% retention. Costs eased—steel $850/ton -8%, hedged 70%; labor +3%. Turns 4.2x, localized semis.

Op margin 13.2%, +110 bps YoY, TTM 12.9%. OpEx 19.6% -50 bps; SAP S/4HANA cut admin 7%, R&D 4.2% on AI PM down 22%, digital twins -15% proto. NA 15.1% shale; EMEA 10.8% wind; APAC 12.4% semis. To 14%+ 2024 via value eng. 200 bps, electric loaders Q1 IRA-eligible, capex 3.8% new plants.

Finally, operating margin guidance: Q3 was 12.8% +110 bps, but for Q4 we guide 13.2-13.6%, +40-80 bps seq., best in five years. Mix to 28% aftermarket via SmartFleet on 45,000 units; Dayton/Monterrey savings $18M, scrap -22%, cycles -15%; +2.5% pricing vs. $850/ton steel. NA infra, EMEA renewables +14% aftermarket, APAC semis +50 bps mix. Offsets: $12M FX, R&D electric drivetrains.

FY24 13.4-13.8%, +90-130 bps vs. 2023 12.5%, $1.2B incr. op income; rev 7-9%, EPS $4.85-5.15, back-half weight 1.15x btb. Cost-outs $75M SG&A, reshore hydro to 12% China; 48V hybrids 2x sales, premium 15%. Risks: rates delay capex, steel $720 spot, but 70% clauses. Toward 15%+ by 2026 on automation/sustainability/digital.

Now, I'll hand over to Raj for an operational update.

Raj Singh (COO):
Thank you, David. Operationally, we've streamlined our supply chain and boosted manufacturing efficiency through new initiatives like advanced automation and digital tech. We've implemented Industry 4.0 upgrades at key plants, improving inventory turns and reducing scrap. We're monitoring global supply chains closely, mitigating disruptions with localized sourcing and vertical integration. Investments in AI predictive maintenance and digital twins are enhancing capabilities across construction, mining, and manufacturing equipment lines.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of rising raw material costs on your profitability?

David Hargrove (CFO):
Good morning, Emily. Raw material costs remain a focus, but we've managed them effectively. Steel stabilized at $850 per ton after earlier spikes, down 8% sequentially, thanks to 70% hedging and multi-year offtakes with suppliers like Nucor. Aluminum and copper eased 5-7% on softer China demand. Pricing actions captured 4-6% across OEM lines, with 2.5% more in Q4, and aftermarket mix at 28% with 35%+ margins provides insulation. Labor up just 3% via incentives and automation. Supply chain localization cut semi risks, improving turns to 4.2x. This flowed through to 32.8% gross margins, and we're guiding Q4 op to 13.2-13.6%. Contingencies in 70% contracts protect against futures volatility at $720 spot. Overall, profitability resilient.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Ben Rodriguez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Rodriguez (Goldman Sachs):
What is your outlook for demand in the aftermarket services business?

Elena Vasquez (CEO):
Thanks, Ben. Aftermarket is a high-margin bright spot, growing 18-22% across segments, now 28% of revenue. Telematics like SmartFleet and Product Link-style platforms on 45,000+ machines drive predictive maintenance, boosting uptake. Mining MRO cycles up 25%, construction utilization 85%, ag precision +14%. Backlog visibility from $4.2B orders, 65% aftermarket gross margins, and digital ARR $520M with 118% NRR ensure recurring strength. Reshoring and electrification sustain 15-20% growth, positioning us for 25% EBITDA expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong (Barclays):
Can you provide an update on your progress in reducing lead times?

Raj Singh (COO):
Thanks, Lisa. Lead times are down to 6-9 months from 12+ peaks, via supply resilience—U.S. castings 40%, Mexico/Poland greenfields, Singapore localization under 8 weeks for APAC. Digital twins cut prototyping 15-30%, AI scheduling throughput +25%, scrap -22%. TitanEdge/IndusEdge on 65% orders enables predictive PM, MTBF double, repairs -35%. ERP digitization 80% order-to-cash, turns 4.2x. Win rate 68%, book-to-bill 1.25x supports on-time delivery 95%, beating peers amid capex rebound.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Elena Vasquez (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in IndusTech Corporation. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Jordan Lee (VP, Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
